subject: Anthropology
title: The Agricultural Revolution
description: Learn The Agricultural Revolution in one minute.

hook.text: For 200,000 years humans hunted and gathered. Then 12,000 years ago, someone planted a seed on purpose.

buildup.text: The Neolithic revolution saw the independent invention of farming in at least seven regions worldwide.

discovery.text: Agriculture allowed food surplus, which enabled permanent settlement, population growth, and social hierarchy.

twist.text: Early farmers were shorter, sicker, and worked longer hours than foragers. Agriculture wasn't obviously better.

climax.text: Farming changed everything: property, inequality, states, and warfare all emerged from the shift to agriculture.

punchline.text: One seed planted the roots of civilization.

quiz.question: What was a consequence of the agricultural revolution?
options: Food surplus enabled hierarchy and permanent settlement

details.summary: The agricultural revolution began roughly 10,000 years ago when humans independently domesticated plants in several world regions. This shift from foraging to farming enabled population growth and social complexity but also brought disease, inequality, environmental degradation, and harder work.
details.whyItMatters: Agriculture is the foundation of civilization — cities, states, writing, and class hierarchy all depend on agricultural surplus. Understanding this transition reveals that human progress is not straightforward — agriculture brought benefits and.
takeaways: Agriculture emerged independently in multiple world regions
It enabled population growth and social complexity
It also brought disease, inequality, and environmental degradation

faq.question: Why did humans switch from foraging to farming?
faq.answer: Climate change at the end of the last Ice Age, population pressure, and resource depletion likely combined. Agriculture may not have been a deliberate choice but a gradual intensification of plant management. Once populations grew dependent on farming, returning to foraging became impossible.

faq.question: Was the agricultural revolution actually beneficial?
faq.answer: It enabled civilization but degraded individual wellbeing. Early farmers were shorter, sicker, and worked harder than foragers. Agriculture created surplus, enabling elites, but also created poverty, famine, and epidemic disease. Jared Diamond called it the worst mistake in human history.
